[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Lakehouse Design Patterns: Mastering the Medallion Architecture with Apache Spark"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Lakehouse architecture combines the best elements of data lakes and data warehouses. At its core is the Medallion Architecture, a data design pattern used to logically organize data in a lakehouse, with the goal of incrementally and progressively improving the structure and quality of data as it flows through each layer of the architecture."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding the Medallion Layers"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Bronze Layer (Raw): Stores raw data ingested from source systems in its original format. Data is typically appended-only and immutable."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Silver Layer (Validated/Enriched): Data from the bronze layer is cleaned, filtered, transformed, and matched. Schema enforcement and data quality checks are applied here."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Gold Layer (Aggregated): Highly refined, aggregated data structured for business intelligence, reporting, and machine learning use cases."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing Bronze to Silver with Apache Spark"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this section, we will read raw JSON data from a bronze table, clean the schema, remove duplicates, and write it to a silver Delta table using Apache Spark."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, current_timestamp

# Initialize Spark Session with Delta support
spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("MedallionArchitectureDemo") \
    .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension") \
    .config("spark.sparkContext.conf", "spark.databricks.delta.sparkCatalog.enabled") \
    .getOrCreate()

# Read from Bronze layer (Raw JSON)
df_bronze = spark.read.json("/mnt/lakehouse/bronze/transactions/")

# Transform to Silver layer: Clean, drop duplicates, and add audit columns
df_silver = df_bronze \
    .filter(col("transaction_id").isNotNull()) \
    .dropDuplicates(["transaction_id"])

# Write to Silver Delta Table
df_silver.write \
    .format("delta") \
    .mode("append") \
    .save("/mnt/lakehouse/silver/transactions/")"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing Silver to Gold Aggregations"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"The gold layer aggregates the clean silver data to generate business-level metrics, such as daily active users or total sales per store."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.sql.functions import sum, avg, to_date

# Read from Silver Delta table
df_silver = spark.read.format("delta").load("/mnt/lakehouse/silver/transactions/")

# Aggregate data for Gold layer
df_gold = df_silver \
    .groupBy(to_date(col("timestamp")).alias("transaction_date"), col("store_id")) \
    .agg(
        sum("amount").alias("total_sales"),
        avg("amount").alias("average_transaction_value")
    )

# Write to Gold Delta Table
df_gold.write \
    .format("delta") \
    .mode("overwrite") \
    .save("/mnt/lakehouse/gold/daily_store_sales/")"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Spark Lakehouse Pipelines"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Delta Lake format to ensure ACID transactions, time travel, and scalable metadata handling."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Optimize and vacuum your Delta tables periodically to maintain high query performance and reduce storage costs."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Implement robust schema evolution policies in your silver pipelines to handle upstream source changes gracefully."}]
